$comment: Withholding tax on compensation tables effective Jan 1, 2023 (RR 11-2018 as amended; BIR revised withholding tax tables). Each bracket: floor (compensation exceeds), base tax, rate on excess over floor.

legalBasis: RR 11-2018 Annex E (Revised Withholding Tax Table effective Jan 1, 2023)
NIRC Sec 24(A)(2)(a) & Sec 79, as amended by RA 10963
tables.notes: Confirmed unchanged through Aug 2026 (no 2024-2026 issuance revised Annex E) and matched against multiple independent sources, including a worked example (₱50,000/mo → ₱1,875 + 20% × ₱16,667 = ₱5,208.40). Withholding applies to taxable compensation after mandatory SSS/PhilHealth/Pag-IBIG employee shares and non-taxable benefits. Pending House/Senate bracket bills would change these tables if enacted (TY2027 earliest).

items.benefit: Employee achievement awards (cash/GC allowed since RR 4-2025)

items.ceiling: 30% of regional basic minimum wage per day

legalBasis: RR 4-2025 (effective Feb 14, 2025: uniform allowance to ₱7,000; cash/GC achievement awards allowed)
deMinimis.notes: RR 29-2025 raised EVERY capped item effective Jan 6, 2026: VL monetization 10→12 days, dependents' medical cash ₱1,500→₱2,000/semester, rice ₱2,000→₱2,500, uniforms ₱7,000→₱8,000 (RR 4-2025 had taken it ₱6,000→₱7,000 in Feb 2025), actual medical ₱10,000→₱12,000, laundry ₱300→₱400, awards ₱10,000→₱12,000 (cash/GC allowed since RR 4-2025), gifts ₱5,000→₱6,000, meal allowance 25%→30%, CBA/productivity ₱10,000→₱12,000. Apply the old ceilings to pre-2026 payroll periods. Amounts within ceilings are tax-free; the excess counts toward the ₱90,000 other-benefits cap.

value.agricultureAndSmallCovers: agriculture, retail/service with 15 or fewer workers and manufacturing with fewer than 10 workers

history.status: implementation enjoined by the Pasig RTC (status quo ante Jul 24, TRO Jul 30, preliminary injunction Aug 13, 2026)

legalBasis: Wage Order No. NCR-28 (₱755 non-agriculture; ₱718 agriculture, retail/service with 15 or fewer workers and manufacturing with fewer than 10 workers; effective Sept 26, 2026)
History: Wage Order NCR-26 (₱695 / ₱658 from July 18, 2025); Wage Order NCR-27 (₱755 / ₱780 in two tranches; implementation enjoined by the Pasig RTC, Jul-Aug 2026)
minimumWageReference.notes: Checked Oct 7, 2026: under Wage Order No. NCR-28 the NCR minimum wage is ₱755 a day for non-agriculture and ₱718 for agriculture, retail/service establishments with 15 or fewer workers and manufacturing establishments with fewer than 10 workers, effective Sept 26, 2026; confirm against the NWPC wage-order PDF (reported by GMA News, Daily Tribune, Philstar, Sept 2026). History: NCR-26 set ₱695 / ₱658 from July 18, 2025; NCR-27's increase (₱755, then ₱780 from Jan 20, 2027) was enjoined by the Pasig RTC (status quo ante Jul 24, TRO Jul 30, preliminary injunction Aug 13, 2026). Every region has its own wage order. The minimum wage earner switch on the Employee and Payroll tabs uses the daily rate you enter, not this reference.

value.method: graduated table on annualized taxable compensation; December adjustment trues up the year

legalBasis: RR 2-98 Sec 2.79(B)(5)(b), as amended by RR 11-2018
annualization.notes: On the last payroll of the year (or on termination), the employer computes tax on the full year's taxable compensation (including pay from a previous employer within the year) using the annual graduated table, and withholds or refunds the difference so total withheld equals annual tax due. Refunds of over-withholding are due to employees not later than January 25 of the following year.

legalBasis: Owner decision 3, Oct 7, 2026 (REVIEW.md 4.3); the rounding instruction on BIR Forms 1601-C and 2316 was not confirmed
payslipRounding.notes: Payslip, withholding and contribution lines are rounded half-up to the centavo (₱3.195 -> ₱3.20), computed exactly in whole centavos, and 12-month totals are 12 × the rounded monthly figure. Confirm against the current 1601-C and 2316 instructions.

legalBasis: NIRC Sec 24(A)(2), as amended by RA 9504 and RA 10963
Soriano v. Secretary of Finance, G.R. No. 184450, Jan 24, 2017
mweExempt.notes: Statutory minimum wage earners (MWEs) are exempt from income tax on their statutory minimum wage, plus holiday pay, overtime pay, night-shift differential and hazard pay, and no tax is withheld on these. Other pay (taxable allowances, commissions) stays taxable, and so do 13th-month pay and other benefits above ₱90,000; receiving them does not cancel the exemption on the minimum wage (Soriano v. Secretary of Finance struck down the RR 10-2008 rule that said it did). The Employee and Payroll calculators apply this when 'Minimum wage earner' is switched on: monthly minimum wage = statutory daily rate × paid days a year (365, 313 or 261) ÷ 12, rounded to the centavo.

mweContributions.value: An MWE's SSS, PhilHealth and Pag-IBIG shares are taken from the tax-free minimum wage, so they do not reduce the taxable other pay
legalBasis: App assumption, Oct 7, 2026, pending CPA confirmation
mweContributions.notes: For a minimum wage earner with other taxable pay, the calculators tax the other pay in full and treat the employee's mandatory contributions as paid out of the exempt minimum wage (the cautious reading: it never shows less tax). Confirm against the BIR Form 2316 and alphalist instructions whether the contributions should instead reduce the taxable other pay.
